title: 就 / 才: early or late, easy or hard
summary: Lets you show something happened sooner or later than expected, as in 他七点就来了 and 他十点才来.
structure: Time + 就 + Verb + 了 (earlier than expected)
Time + 才 + Verb (later than expected, no 了)
explanation:
就 and 才 go after a time word and before the verb, and they add the speaker's feeling. 就 = 'already, as early as': 他七点就来了 'He came as early as seven.' It usually has 了. 才 = 'not until, only then': 他十点才来 'He didn't come until ten.' 才 never takes 了.

就 also means 'right away, then': 我就来 'I'm coming right now', 你去，我就去 'If you go, I'll go'.

examples.en: He came as early as seven.
I didn't go to bed until twelve last night.

examples.zh: 八点上课，他七点就到了。
examples.en: Class is at eight; he was there by seven.

mistakes.why: 就 goes after the time word, before the verb.

exercises.en: Class starts at 8, but she arrived at 7 (early!).
why: Correct: earlier than expected = 就 … 了.

exercises.en: He didn't get up until eleven.
why: Correct: later than expected = 才, with no 了.
就 would mean he got up early.
Correct: time + 才 + verb, no 了.
才 goes after the time expression, right before the verb.

exercises.instruction: Show it was EARLIER than expected.
why: Correct: time + 就 + verb + 了.
就 goes after the time word.

exercises.en: I didn't finish my homework until ten.
exercises.why: Time + 才 + verb, with no 了.

exercises.prompt: Your friend calls: dinner is ready. You say 'Coming!':
why: 才来 means 'only now coming' and sounds like a complaint.
